From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Lighthouse Therapeutics — private deploy intake & network acceptance (initial checklist)

Hi Ava / ACME team —

Thanks again for the kick-off earlier this week. Attached is a concise intake & acceptance checklist we typically use to accelerate VPC/on-prem private deployments while preserving auditability. This thread will track network and account-level prerequisites so ops and security can sign off before we move to provisioning.

Key items we need from your side to move into provisioning:
- AWS account IDs (management & workload) or on-prem cluster IP range + owner
- VPC CIDR preference (if you have multiple envs: prod/stage sandbox)
- Static egress IP addresses (or NAT gateway plan) for allowlisting outbound traffic
- KMS key ARN or guidance if you want Redwood to use a cross-account CMK (we need key policy and encryption requirements)
- Firewall rules / port allowlist for control-plane and runtime: recommended ports in the attached checklist (please return a completed allowlist CSV)
- Point of contact for certificate provisioning and DNS delegation (we need a CNAME for telemetry & callback endpoints)

Proposed next milestones:
1) You return the completed checklist + firewall allowlist by EOD Fri 6/20
2) We validate account and peering prerequisites 6/23 — 6/24
3) Provisioning window (non-production smoke) 6/25 03:00–06:00 UTC — please confirm a maintenance window

Attachments: lighthouse_onboarding_checklist_v1.xlsx; network-diagram-v1.png

If anything in the checklist is a blocker for your team, call it out explicitly and we'll surface an exception or alternate plan.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Technical Program Manager
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jun 18, 2025 at 08:12 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ava / ACME team —
> 
> Thanks again for the kick-off earlier this week. Attached is a concise intake & acceptance checklist we typically use...

Quick clarifications from infra side:
- For the egress IPs we usually prefer either a small static range (<= /29) or a NAT with Elastic IPs. If Lighthouse plans to use a proxy appliance, include that as an alternate and we will work with your netops to open the ipsec/express routes.
- KMS: if you want Redwood to encrypt with a customer-managed key, we need an explicit cross-account policy. If you don't have a CMK yet we can proceed with our managed key for the smoke test but require a migration plan before production.
- DNS: we will provide a telemetry CNAME (telemetry.redwood-callbacks.lighthouse.example.com) — confirm if your DNS team can add that record under the delegated zone.

I'll add two short items to the acceptance checklist: a) expected sequence lengths for smoke traffic (we'll validate token sizes) b) a TTL expectation for the allowlist (some customers want a two-week rolling window).

Ben Carter
Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: none (see Naomi's checklist)

Thanks for the checklist — we've completed and attached the firewall allowlist (firewall-allowlist.csv) and answered the intake fields in the Excel. Summary answers here:
- AWS accounts: management 123456789012, workloads 210987654321 (we are using separate accounts per environment)
- VPC CIDRs: prod 10.10.0.0/16, stage 10.11.0.0/16, sandbox 10.12.0.0/20
- Egress: We can allocate two Elastic IPs for Nexthop NAT (54.23.11.7, 54.23.11.8) — please confirm these are sufficient
- KMS: we will provision a customer-managed key and provide ARN before prod. For staging/sandbox you may use Redwood-managed key
- DNS: DNS is managed at lighthouse-ops.example.com; our DNS owner (ops@lighthouse-thera.com) can add the CNAME once you provide it

We are targeting the smoke window on 6/25 as proposed. We do have a short maintenance freeze 6/26–6/27, so keep that in mind for any follow-ups.

Attachments: firewall-allowlist.csv

Let us know if you need the CIDR split expanded or a direct peering diagram.

Best,

Thanks Ava — this is great and clear. Next steps from Redwood: 
- Ben and Karthik will validate the two EIPs against our egress allowlist and confirm NAT configuration (by EOD 6/21).
- We will post the telemetry CNAME and a short runbook for certificate exchange to the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-onboarding-docs) by COB 6/21.
- Please provide the CMK ARN for prod by 6/24 so we can include it in the production provisioning plan.

Go/no-go criteria for the smoke window (6/25):
- Completed and accepted firewall allowlist
- Egress IPs validated and reachable from control plane
- DNS CNAME in place for telemetry callbacks OR alternate webhook target provided
- Short smoke run: 1k tokens aggregated traffic across three clients without certificate errors

I've created an internal ticket (HS-42317) to track infra validation and evidence collection — I will update the ticket with Ben/Karthik notes after their validation pass.

If we hit any blocker from security (e.g., CMK not available) we'll run a controlled smoke with Redwood-managed keys and re-run encryption migration for prod.

Thanks all — I'll follow up with the runbook and the procurement checklist pointers.
